title: Sovereign AI Index 2026: National Models, Compute and Who Uses Them
dek: 58 national and sovereign AI models across 31 countries and regions, the compute programmes behind them, and the evidence on whether anyone uses them: downloads, users, leaderboard ranks and home-market share. Every figure dated, sourced and confidence-rated.

at_a_glance: We catalogue 58 sovereign or national AI model families across 31 countries and regions. About 40 are described as trained from scratch and about 13 are adaptations of foreign open-weight models such as Meta's Llama, Google's Gemma, Alibaba's Qwen or Nvidia's Nemotron.

Measured by developer downloads, sovereign models are a niche: in the 30 days to 12 November 2026, 31 national model makers together recorded about 13.6 million Hugging Face downloads, about 5.8% of the 234.5 million for Alibaba's Qwen alone (Report AI calculation from Hugging Face data). France's Mistral accounts for most of that national total.

Measured by capability, the frontier is American and Chinese: 15 of the top 20 models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0.1, November 2026) come from US developers and 5 from Chinese ones. The best-scoring model from any other country is Mistral Large 4, at 26.1 against 64.6 for the leader.

Measured by home-market use, local champions win only where foreign assistants are blocked or weak: in China, ByteDance's Doubao had 419 million monthly users in September 2026; in South Korea, ChatGPT had about 91% of AI-app users despite years of investment in local models.

The money is mostly going into compute rather than models: national programmes in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, India, Japan, South Korea, Canada and the EU buy chips and data centres, then run a mix of imported and local models on them.
analysis: Sovereign AI has become one of the most used phrases in AI policy and one of the least defined. For this index we separate four things that are often run together: sovereign infrastructure (domestic compute under national control), sovereign models (trained from scratch or adapted from foreign open weights), sovereign data (control over national training corpora) and sovereign deployment (foreign models run in-country under local rules). Most countries pursue all four in name and fund mainly the first.

The popularity evidence is sobering for national models. On Hugging Face, the main distribution channel for open models, Chinese models took 41% of downloads between February 2025 and February 2026, ahead of US models, and Alibaba's Qwen alone outdraws every national model maker combined many times over. National models do find users where they serve a language or a regulated sector that global models serve poorly: Japanese government trials, Korean public services, Arabic-language deployments and Indian-language speech. But outside China and Russia, where policy or sanctions shape the market, no national assistant leads its home consumer market.

That does not make sovereign programmes pointless. Their realistic product is resilience and bargaining power rather than market share: domestic compute that keeps running if access is cut off, models that can be audited and adapted for public services, and the skills to do both. The June 2026 suspension of two US frontier models under export controls, and China's October 2026 draft controls on model weights, showed why governments value that. The risk is the one visible in our data: adapted models built on Qwen, Llama or Gemma inherit their base model's licence and, potentially, its home country's export rules.

The compute build-out is also slower than the headlines. Stargate UAE had no capacity operating in November 2026; Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN's '600,000 GPUs' is a three-year ceiling against signed deals for about 27,000; and India's common compute portal had onboarded about 38,000 GPUs by March 2026, roughly the figure it reported six months earlier.
takeaways: Separate the layers: infrastructure, models, data and deployment are different kinds of sovereignty.
Most national models are adaptations of foreign open weights, chiefly Llama, Gemma, Qwen and Nemotron.
Downloads, users and leaderboard ranks all show national models as niche outside China.
Home-market leadership by a domestic assistant happens where foreign assistants are blocked or restricted.
Announced compute (GW, GPU ceilings) runs well ahead of operating compute.

chapters.action_title: Sovereign AI is four different things, and most programmes fund infrastructure first
paras: The typology below is used throughout this index. It draws on definitions from Stanford HAI, CSET, CNAS, McKinsey and Counterpoint Research, simplified into categories that can be measured.

tables.title: A typology of sovereign AI
rows: A state's capacity to develop, run and govern AI on infrastructure, data and models it controls, rather than renting them from foreign providers. Definitions are contested: 'hard' sovereignty means self-sufficiency across the stack; 'soft' sovereignty means control over the layers that matter for a given use case.
Domestic data centres and GPU clusters under national legal control, funded by budgets, state banks or sovereign-wealth vehicles.
IndiaAI common compute (38,231 GPUs); Isambard-AI (UK); ABCI 3.0 (Japan); JUPITER (EU)
Foundation models pre-trained from random initialisation by a national lab or champion.
Falcon (UAE); Jais 2 (UAE); K2 Think V2 (UAE); ALLaM 34B (Saudi)
Sovereign models - adapted (continued pre-training / fine-tune of foreign open weights)
A national model built on a foreign open-weight base (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, Nemotron) with local data.
SEA-LION v4 (Gemma 3; Qwen variant); Fanar 2.0 (Gemma-3-27B); KazLLM (Llama); Latam-GPT (Llama 3.1)
Foreign proprietary or open models run in-country under local data residency, often via 'sovereign cloud' offers.
Japan's 'Gennai' government AI (OpenAI-powered, now A/B-testing domestic LLMs); SoftBank Cloud PF Type A on Oracle Alloy; Cohere on Bell AI Fabric (Canada)
Legal and practical control over national training corpora and the data pipeline (licensed national-library, news and administrative text).
GPT-NL licensed news + KB national library; Viettel administrative/regulatory corpora; TAIDE government documents; Jais 2's 600B Arabic tokens
Public money behind the stack: budgets/appropriations, equity funds, sovereign-wealth vehicles, and mobilisation headlines - four categories that must never be summed.
IndiaAI Mission (budget); China National AI Fund (equity); HUMAIN, MGX (sovereign vehicles); EU InvestAI EUR 200B (mobilisation)
Markets where foreign assistants are blocked or restricted, so domestic models dominate regardless of policy intent.
China: Doubao 419M MAU, Qwen 158M, DeepSeek 123M (Sep 2026); Russia (sanctions): domestic share depends on measurement method
Popularity metrics (and why they cannot be compared)

Hugging Face downloads (developer pulls, inflated by CI/mirrors), derivatives (fine-tunes on a base), app MAU/WAU (consumer reach; panels disagree), web-traffic share, Statcounter referral share (clicks from chatbots to websites), OpenRouter token share (one developer aggregator), leaderboard rank (capability, not use).

chapters.action_title: National model makers together draw about 6% of the downloads of Alibaba's Qwen alone
paras: Hugging Face downloads are the most complete public measure of open-model popularity, though they count developers and automated systems rather than end users. In the 30 days to 12 November 2026, the Qwen organisation recorded about 234.5 million downloads. The 31 national and sovereign model makers we track recorded about 13.6 million between them, and France's Mistral alone accounted for about 60% of that (Report AI calculation).

Over longer windows the pattern is the same. The ATOM project's count of cumulative downloads put Qwen at about 942 million by March 2026, roughly twice Meta's Llama, and Hugging Face reported that Chinese models took 41% of all downloads between February 2025 and February 2026. Qwen is also the most popular base for national adaptations, which means part of the 'sovereign' ecosystem in Southeast Asia and elsewhere now runs on a Chinese foundation.

chapters.action_title: On capability leaderboards and developer platforms, the US and China take almost every top spot
paras: On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0.1, 12 November 2026), the top nine models are all from US developers, led by Claude Fable 5.2 at 64.6; the best Chinese model is Kimi K3.1 Pro at 46.5, the highest-ranked open-weight model. The best model from any third country is Mistral Large 4 from France at 26.1, followed by the UAE's K2 Horizon (17.8) and South Korea's Solar Pro 4 (14.2). No model from India, Japan, Russia or Germany appears on the index.

On OpenRouter, a developer marketplace that routes requests to many models, Chinese developers took about 47% of requests in the week beginning 2 November 2026 and US developers about 39% (Report AI calculation by developer country); DeepSeek alone had about 32%. OpenRouter notes that its rankings measure traffic through its own platform, not users or spending. LMArena's crowd-sourced rankings could not be verified for this edition.

chapters.action_title: Domestic assistants lead their home markets only where foreign ones are blocked or restricted
paras: The consumer test of sovereignty is whether people at home choose the national assistant. In China, where Western assistants are blocked, domestic apps dominate: ByteDance's Doubao had about 419 million monthly users in September 2026, Alibaba's Qianwen about 158 million and DeepSeek about 123 million (QuestMobile). In Russia, Yandex's Alice AI reached about 48% of people aged 12 and over in September 2026, against 5% for Sber's GigaChat (Mediascope).

Elsewhere, global assistants lead even in countries with strong national programmes. In South Korea, ChatGPT's app had 18.76 million monthly users in October 2026, about 91% of AI-app users, and Naver closed its standalone chatbot in April 2026 to focus on AI answers inside search. In France, ChatGPT dominates consumer use while Mistral's strength is in enterprise and government contracts. In India, OpenAI said in November 2026 that the country had become ChatGPT's largest market.

chapters.action_title: Announced sovereign compute runs well ahead of what is operating
paras: Most sovereign money buys infrastructure. The table lists the main national programmes with their headline and, where available, delivered figures. Four kinds of money appear and should never be added together: budget appropriations, state equity funds, sovereign-wealth vehicles, and 'mobilisation' headlines that count expected private investment.

Delivery lags announcement. Epoch AI's data-centre tracking shows Stargate UAE with no capacity operating in November 2026, against a first 200 MW projected for December. HUMAIN's 600,000-GPU figure is a three-year ceiling; its signed October 2026 deal covers about 27,000 GPUs and 84 MW through 2027. Nvidia, the clearest commercial proxy, reported more than $30 billion of sovereign AI revenue in its fiscal 2026 and has given only growth rates since.

stop_quoting.claim: Perplexity holds about 48% of Russia's AI-chatbot market (because it stayed accessible while rivals restricted access).
stop_quoting.fact: [11 Nov ET verification] The number has a source but the framing is wrong. Statcounter recorded Perplexity at 47.92% of AI-chatbot-referred page views in Russia in April 2026 (all platforms), but Statcounter measures clicks from chatbots through to websites, not market share or users; Perplexity fell to 21.33% in September 2026 and was 39.34% in October 2026, when Gemini had 32.44% and ChatGPT 23.38%. Statcounter does not track GigaChat or Alice AI at all. Web-traffic data for 2025 put ChatGPT near 40% and DeepSeek at 27.8%. The access-restriction explanation is not supported by any source found.

stop_quoting.claim: South Korea runs on Naver's HyperCLOVA X / HyperCLOVA X is Korea's most-used AI model.
stop_quoting.fact: Naver closed its standalone Clova X chatbot in April 2026, and Korea's ministry dropped Naver Cloud from the national foundation-model project on 15 January 2026. ChatGPT's Korean app had 18.76 million monthly users in October 2026 (Mobile Index), about 91% of AI-app users. HyperCLOVA X's reach is through Naver search: AI Briefing ~30 million monthly users (May 2026). [11 Nov ET verification] Statcounter (Oct 2026) shows Gemini 65.25% and ChatGPT 23.62% of chatbot-referred page views in Korea and does not track Naver. On Hugging Face the official naver-hyperclovax org logged 33,507 downloads in 30 days vs 724,713 for LG's LGAI-EXAONE.

No evidence of government adoption was found. Japan's Digital Agency began trialling three domestic LLMs on its 'Gennai' platform in July 2026: NTT's tsuzumi 2, Fujitsu's Takane 32B and PFN's PLaMo 2.0 Prime. [11 Nov ET verification] Hugging Face: the Fugaku-LLM org's 3 repos logged 24 downloads in the last 30 days (14,584 all-time).

stop_quoting.claim: India is OpenAI's second-largest ChatGPT market.
stop_quoting.fact: True in February 2026 (100 million weekly users). On 3 November 2026 OpenAI's India managing director said India had become ChatGPT's largest market by weekly active users, with the user base doubling since January.
34,000+ was the May-June 2025 count. 38,231 GPUs were onboarded by 25 March 2026 (Lok Sabha), and the IT minister announced 20,000 more in February 2026; the end-2026 target is 100,000.

stop_quoting.claim: Falcon models have been downloaded 45 million times.
stop_quoting.fact: TII has since reported 55 million+ downloads across the Falcon ecosystem (2025); its Q1 2024 figure was 43 million. [11 Nov ET verification] Hugging Face API: TII's 137 public repos total 68.7M all-time downloads and 378,202 in the last 30 days (12 Nov 2026).

stop_quoting.claim: Mistral AI is valued at $14 billion.
stop_quoting.fact: That was the September 2025 Series C (EUR 11.7B). Mistral's EUR 3 billion Series D on 8 September 2026 valued it at more than EUR 21 billion post-money (~US$24B).

stop_quoting.claim: Le Chat is Mistral's consumer assistant.
stop_quoting.fact: Mistral renamed Le Chat to Vibe on 28 May 2026; quote the new name with 'formerly Le Chat'.

stop_quoting.claim: Aleph Alpha is Germany's independent sovereign AI champion.
stop_quoting.fact: Canada's Cohere agreed to acquire Aleph Alpha (announced 24 April 2026); the combined group keeps the Cohere name and Aleph Alpha shareholders hold about 10%.

stop_quoting.claim: Stargate UAE is live / went live in 2026.
stop_quoting.fact: Epoch AI's satellite-based tracking shows 0 MW operational at Stargate UAE as of November 2026, with the first two 100 MW buildings projected for December 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN is deploying 600,000 Nvidia GPUs.
stop_quoting.fact: 600,000 is an 'up to' ceiling over three years across Saudi Arabia and the US. The deal HUMAIN signed in October 2026 covers up to 84 MW and about 27,000 GPUs through 2027, starting with ~6,000 B300s in Q4 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: Most national 'sovereign' models are home-grown from scratch.
stop_quoting.fact: Counterpoint's H1 2026 index found 56% of sovereign LLMs are adapted from foreign bases (Llama 38%, Qwen 20%, Mistral 19% of those). CNAS puts from-scratch models at about 40% of tracked model projects (Aug 2026).

stop_quoting.claim: Chinese models take 61% of OpenRouter tokens.
stop_quoting.fact: 61% is the Chinese share among the top-10 models only, Feb-Mar 2026. Platform-wide snapshots in April 2026 showed ~51%, and Chinese models' share of US enterprise traffic was 30-46% weekly. [11 Nov ET verification] See the newer verified entry (week of 2 Nov 2026).

stop_quoting.claim: Doubao has 382 million users; Qwen's app 167 million.
stop_quoting.fact: Those are May-June 2026 readings. QuestMobile's September 2026 figures: Doubao 419.08 million MAU, Qwen app 158.17 million (down), DeepSeek 122.65 million.

stop_quoting.claim: The EU is building four AI gigafactories with EUR 20 billion.
stop_quoting.fact: No site has been chosen. The formal EuroHPC call for up to seven gigafactories closed on 12 November 2026, with awards expected in early 2027; public funding reported at EUR 10 billion plus ~EUR 20 billion hoped-for private money.
Sources disagree on whether 600,000 refers to users or to requests; ISSAI reports 140,000+ downloads. Quote neither as 'users' without the caveat.

stop_quoting.claim: StatCounter shows ChatGPT's (or any chatbot's) market share in a country.
stop_quoting.fact: [11 Nov ET verification] Statcounter's AI-chatbot series counts page views on Statcounter-tracked websites that were referred by a chatbot (clicks out of answers), based on ~3 billion monthly page views. It is not users, prompts or sessions, it tracks only six global assistants (no Doubao, GigaChat, Alice, Naver, Le Chat), and October 2026 shows a series-wide break (ChatGPT worldwide 80.47% Sep -> 51.03% Oct).

stop_quoting.claim: Two Chinese models sit in the global top four (Artificial Analysis).
stop_quoting.fact: [11 Nov ET verification] On Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (12 Nov 2026) the nine highest-scoring distinct models are all from US labs; the best Chinese model is Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro at 46.5 (#10, the top open-weights model). The September readings (Qwen3.8-Max 58, Kimi K3 57.1) were on an earlier index version and are not comparable.

stop_quoting.claim: Chinese models are 61% of OpenRouter traffic.
stop_quoting.fact: [11 Nov ET verification] Latest complete week (from 2 Nov 2026): Chinese authors had 47.2% of text requests (DeepSeek 31.8%, Z.ai 7.4%, Qwen 5.7%, Tencent 2.3%) vs 38.7% for OpenAI, Google and Anthropic; by tokens, Chinese models are 83.4% of the top-10 models' volume. State the metric (requests vs tokens) and the week.

faq.a: Sovereign AI is a country's capacity to develop, run and govern AI on infrastructure, data and models it controls, rather than renting them from foreign providers. In practice it covers four layers: domestic compute, national models (from scratch or adapted), control of training data, and in-country deployment of foreign models under local rules.

faq.q: Which countries have built their own AI models?
faq.a: Report AI's November 2026 index catalogues 58 national model families across 31 countries and regions, including France (Mistral), the UAE (Falcon, Jais, K2), Saudi Arabia (ALLaM), India (Sarvam, BharatGen), Japan (PLaMo, LLM-jp, tsuzumi), South Korea (EXAONE, A.X, Solar), Switzerland (Apertus), Singapore (SEA-LION), Russia (GigaChat, Alice AI) and China (Qwen, DeepSeek, Doubao, Kimi, GLM).

Mostly not, outside China. In the 30 days to 12 November 2026, 31 national model makers together had about 13.6 million Hugging Face downloads, about 5.8% of Alibaba's Qwen alone, and no model from outside the US and China ranks in the top 20 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

faq.q: What is the most popular sovereign AI model?
faq.a: By home-market users, China's Doubao (ByteDance) with about 419 million monthly users in September 2026. Among models outside the US and China, France's Mistral leads on developer downloads and capability scores.

faq.q: How much are governments spending on sovereign AI?
faq.a: Announced figures run to hundreds of billions, but they mix budgets, state funds, sovereign-wealth vehicles and private 'mobilisation' totals that cannot be added together. Delivered compute is much smaller: Stargate UAE had no capacity operating in November 2026, and India's common compute portal had about 38,000 GPUs onboarded by March 2026.

methodology_extra: The catalogue was compiled from developer announcements, model cards and national programme documents. Popularity measures come from the Hugging Face API (organisation download totals, read 12 November 2026), Artificial Analysis (Intelligence Index v5.0.1), OpenRouter's public rankings, StatCounter, and national app and audience trackers (QuestMobile, Mediascope, Mobile Index). Each measures something different; none is a count of users across all channels. Shares of downloads and requests by country, and counts of models by build type, are Report AI calculations (DERIVED).
